subject: Chemistry
name: Theory (Core)
description: Core theory covering compounds and mixtures, petroleum fractionation, air pollutants, states of matter, metals and extraction, rate of reaction, organic chemistry, and electrolysis of ionic compounds.

parts.label: a
parts.question: A list of compounds: ammonia, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, cobalt(II) chloride, ethane, ethene, glucose, methane, potassium sulfate, sodium phosphate, sulfur dioxide. Give the name of the compound that is an unsaturated hydrocarbon.

parts.label: b
parts.question: Give the name of the compound that leads to the deoxygenation of water in rivers.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Give the name of the compound that is a gas which turns damp red litmus paper blue.

parts.label: d
parts.question: Give the name of the compound that is the main constituent of natural gas.

parts.label: e
parts.question: Give the name of the compound that is a product of photosynthesis.

parts.label: f
parts.question: Give the name of the compound that is a compound of a transition element.

parts.label: a
parts.question: Petroleum is a mixture of hydrocarbons. Describe two characteristics of a mixture.

parts.label: b(i)
parts.question: Fig. 2.1 shows a fractionating column with fractions: refinery gas (top), gasoline, A, kerosene, diesel oil, fuel oil, lubricating oil, bitumen (bottom). Draw an X inside the column to show where the hydrocarbon with the lowest volatility collects.

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.question: Name the fraction labelled A (between gasoline and kerosene) in the fractionating column.

parts.label: b(iii)
parts.question: State the name of the fraction which has hydrocarbons with the longest chain length.

parts.label: b(iv)
parts.question: State one use of the fuel oil fraction.

parts.label: a(i)
parts.question: Table 3.1 shows average concentrations (ng/1000 cm³) of air pollutants over four years: 2019 (CO 2.5, HC 12.0, NOx 19.6, particulates 28.0, SO₂ 30.0); 2020 (CO 2.0, HC 13.5, NOx 21.8, particulates 30.1, SO₂ 21.7); 2021 (CO 1.8, HC 14.8, NOx 18.5, particulates 27.5, SO₂ 23.8); 2022 (CO 1.6, HC 16.0, NOx 22.7, particulates 26.2, SO₂ 25.0). Name the oxide pollutant that has the highest concentration in 2021.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.question: Name the pollutant that shows a continuous decrease in concentration from 2019 to 2022.

parts.label: a(iii)
parts.question: Calculate the average mass, in ng, of particulates in a 250 cm³ sample of polluted air in 2019. (Particulates in 2019: 28.0 ng per 1000 cm³.)

parts.label: b(i)
parts.question: State one adverse effect of particulates on health.

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.question: Particulates are formed by the incomplete combustion of hydrocarbons. State the meaning of the term incomplete combustion.

parts.label: c(i)
parts.question: Oxides of nitrogen contribute to acid rain. Choose the pH value for an acidic solution. Circle your answer.

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.question: Complete the sentence about removing oxides of nitrogen from car exhausts using two words from the list: agent, catalytic, compound, converter, distillation, filter, oxidising, pump. The emission of oxides of nitrogen from car exhausts is reduced by using a .............................. .............................. .

parts.label: c(iii)
parts.question: Oxides of nitrogen can be formed by the action of bacteria on nitrates. Name the aqueous solution and the metal used in the test for nitrate ions.

parts.label: d(i)
parts.question: Nitrogen dioxide decomposes when heated to produce nitric oxide and oxygen. Complete the symbol equation: .....NO₂ ⇋ 2NO + ...........

parts.label: d(ii)
parts.question: State the meaning of the symbol ⇋ in the equation.

parts.label: a
parts.question: Tin is a solid at room temperature. State two general properties of a solid.

parts.label: b
parts.question: Fig. 4.1 shows changes of state: solid tin → (A) → liquid tin → (B) → tin gas. Name the changes of physical states A and B.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Describe solid and liquid tin in terms of the separation and motion of the particles.

parts.label: d
parts.question: A sealed gas syringe contains 80 cm³ of carbon dioxide gas. State how decreasing the temperature affects the volume of CO₂ when the pressure remains constant.

parts.label: a(i)
parts.question: Table 5.1 shows Group I metal properties: Li (mp 181°C, bp 1342°C, atomic vol 12.9 cm³/mol), Na (mp 98°C, atomic vol 23.7, bubbles rapidly, no flame), K (mp 63°C, bp 760°C, atomic vol 45.4, bubbles rapidly and flame), Rb (mp 39°C, bp 686°C, explodes). Predict the boiling point of sodium.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.question: Predict the atomic volume of rubidium.

parts.label: a(iii)
parts.question: Predict the observations when lithium reacts with water.

parts.label: a(iv)
parts.question: Predict the physical state of lithium at 1300°C. Give a reason for your answer.

parts.label: b(i)
parts.question: Iron is extracted in a blast furnace: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂. Explain how this equation shows that iron(III) oxide is reduced.

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.question: Choose the phrase which describes the meaning of (III) in iron(III) oxide. Tick one box.
options: the number of oxygen atoms in iron(III) oxide
the oxidation number of iron in iron(III) oxide
the number of CO molecules which react
the number of electrons in one atom of iron

parts.label: b(iii)
parts.question: Calcium carbonate is added to the blast furnace and undergoes thermal decomposition. Complete the word equation: calcium carbonate → ........................ + ........................

parts.label: c(i)
parts.question: Stainless steel is an alloy. Fig. 5.1 shows four diagrams A, B, C, D of atomic arrangements. Choose the diagram that best shows the structure of an alloy (different sized atoms mixed in a regular lattice).

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.question: Give one reason for using stainless steel instead of pure iron for cutlery.

parts.label: d
parts.question: Table 5.2 shows observations of four metals with dilute HCl: iron (bubbles slowly), mercury (no bubbles), strontium (bubbles very quickly), tin (bubbles very slowly). Put the metals in order of reactivity, least reactive first.

parts.label: a(i)
parts.question: Fig. 6.1 shows volume of hydrogen gas vs time for magnesium with excess HCl at 20°C (curve rising and levelling off at ~50 cm³ by 80s). Deduce the volume of hydrogen gas released after 30 seconds.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.question: The experiment is repeated using smaller pieces of magnesium with the same mass. All other conditions stay the same. Draw a line on the grid to show the volume of hydrogen gas released. (Describe: steeper initial slope, same final volume, reaches endpoint sooner.)

parts.label: b(i)
parts.question: The experiment is repeated at a higher temperature of 35°C. All other conditions stay the same. Describe how the rate of reaction differs.

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.question: The experiment is repeated using a lower concentration of acid. All other conditions stay the same. Describe how the rate of reaction differs.

parts.label: c(i)
parts.question: Complete the word equation for the reaction of hydrochloric acid with lithium hydroxide. hydrochloric acid + lithium hydroxide → ........................ + ........................

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.question: Choose from the list the word that best describes this reaction. Circle your answer.

parts.label: c(iii)
parts.question: State the colour of a solution of thymolphthalein dissolved in aqueous sodium hydroxide.

parts.label: a(i)
parts.question: Fig. 7.1 shows the displayed formula of fumaric acid (HOOC-CH=CH-COOH, a molecule with a C=C double bond and two COOH groups). On the diagram, draw a circle around one carboxylic acid functional group.

parts.label: a(ii)
parts.question: Deduce the molecular formula of fumaric acid (4 carbons, 4 hydrogens, 4 oxygens).

parts.label: a(iii)
parts.question: Fumaric acid is a colourless compound. Describe the colour change when excess fumaric acid is added to aqueous bromine.

parts.label: b
parts.question: Fumaric acid can be oxidised to produce C₄H₆O₆. Complete Table 7.1 to calculate Mr. C: 4×12=48, H: 6×1=6, O: 6×16=96. Find Mr.

parts.label: c
parts.question: Complete the word equation for the reaction of ethanoic acid with sodium carbonate. ethanoic acid + sodium carbonate → ........................ + ........................ + ........................

parts.label: d(i)
parts.question: Ethanoic acid can be produced by the oxidation of ethanol. State one use of ethanol.

parts.label: d(ii)
parts.question: Ethanol, C₂H₅OH, is an alcohol. Choose the general formula for the alcohol homologous series. Circle your answer.

parts.label: d(iii)
parts.question: Ethanol can be manufactured by the addition of steam to ethene. State two conditions for this reaction.

parts.label: a
parts.question: Zinc chloride is an ionic compound. Ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten or in aqueous solution. Describe one other physical property of ionic compounds.

parts.label: b
parts.question: Complete Fig. 8.1 to show the electronic configuration of a chloride ion (Cl, atomic number 17) and the charge on the ion. Cl⁻ has 18 electrons, configuration 2,8,8, charge 1–.

parts.label: c(i)
parts.question: Deduce the number of protons and neutrons in the zinc ion ⁶⁷Zn²⁺ (atomic number 30).

parts.label: d
parts.question: Molten zinc chloride is electrolysed using graphite electrodes. State the names of the products at each electrode and give the observations at the positive electrode.

parts.label: e(i)
parts.question: Graphite electrodes conduct electricity. State one other property that the graphite electrode should have.

parts.label: e(ii)
parts.question: Choose the correct statement about the structure and bonding in graphite. Tick one box.

parts.label: e(iii)
parts.question: State one use of graphite other than as an electrode.
